claimBoundary: This is one provenance-bound Codex pass. It is single-model evidence, not human, instructor, independent, classroom, or multi-judge validation.

claims: Recursion solves a problem by reducing it to a simpler version of the same problem; a recursive function calls itself on a smaller input until it reaches a base case.
A recursive function calls itself on a smaller input.
The process continues until the problem is small enough that the solution is known or easily found — the base case.
Without a base case that stops the self-calls, recursion never terminates and overflows the call stack.
attribution: OpenStax Introduction to Python Programming, §12.1 Recursion basics

artifact.df: The stopping condition that makes the answer known or easy to find.
artifact.eg: A recursive list function returns immediately when the list is empty.
artifact.mi: It is the step that makes the problem larger.
artifact.cx: The recursive calls handle smaller inputs; the base case ends the chain.

artifact.df: The specific state or input size that halts the recursive process.
artifact.eg: In a factorial function, the input being 0 is the termination condition.
artifact.mi: Believing that any self-call guarantees termination.
artifact.cx: The termination condition is the base case, which is the point where the solution is known or easily found.

claims: A variable is a name that refers to a stored value; the assignment operator = binds the name on the left to the value produced on the right (for objects it binds the reference, so no copy is made).
A statement sets a variable to a value using the assignment operator (=), with the name on the left and the value on the right.
Assignment is not mathematical equality — = copies a value into a variable rather than asserting two sides are equal.
A variable name may contain letters, digits, and underscores and be any length, but cannot start with a digit.
Variable names are case-sensitive, so total and Total are two different variables.
attribution: OpenStax Introduction to Python Programming, §1.3 Variables

artifact.df: A label used to access a stored value in memory, such as `count` in a loop.
artifact.eg: If `data = [1, 2, 3]`, `data` is the name referring to the list stored in memory.
artifact.mi: Thinking the name itself is the stored value.
artifact.cx: The name is a reference to the stored value.

artifact.df: A named reference to a stored value; the name points to a value already in memory.
artifact.mi: A variable is the value itself, not a name.
artifact.cx: The correction is that the name refers to the stored value, so later code can use the name to access it.

claims: A list is an ordered collection of values written in square brackets; each element has an index, beginning at 0.
A list is written with square brackets [] holding comma-separated values.
Individual elements are accessed directly using an index.
Indexes begin at 0 and end at one less than the length of the sequence.
A for loop can iterate through a list, visiting each element in order.
attribution: OpenStax Introduction to Python Programming, §3.4 List basics; §9.1 Modifying and iterating lists

artifact.df: The technique used to retrieve a specific item from the collection.
artifact.eg: Using the index to get the second item in a list.
artifact.mi: Using a key to retrieve an item from a list.
artifact.cx: Individual elements are accessed directly using an index because individual elements are accessed directly using an index.

artifact.df: The punctuation used to write a list and hold its values.
artifact.eg: [3, 5, 7] is a list written with square brackets.
artifact.mi: They are only for indexing, not for writing the list itself.
artifact.cx: The same brackets are used to write the list form directly.

claims: The rock cycle describes how Earth's three rock families — igneous, sedimentary, and metamorphic — form and continually transform into one another through geologic processes.
The rock cycle describes the major Earth materials, the processes that form them, and how they relate to each other.
Igneous rock forms when liquid rock freezes solid; lithified sediment becomes sedimentary rock; pre-existing rock can transform into metamorphic rock.
If conditions melt the rocks into magma, the cycle begins anew with new igneous rocks.
attribution: An Introduction to Geology (opengeology.org), §4 The rock cycle

artifact.q: Which process is central to the rock cycle as described in the source material?
op: D) Ordering events in geologic time
artifact.ex: Option C is correct because the rock cycle describes how the three rock families form and transform into one another. Option A is a separate process related to surface change, and Option B is only one step in the cycle.

artifact.q: A student heats a buried sedimentary rock until minerals recrystallize without melting. Which rock family best fits the product?
artifact.ex: The best choice is metamorphic rock because pre-existing rock can transform into metamorphic rock. A common misconception is to call any altered rock igneous, but igneous rock requires liquid rock to freeze solid; here, the rock changed without melting.

claims: The rock cycle describes how Earth's three rock families — igneous, sedimentary, and metamorphic — form and continually transform into one another through geologic processes.
The rock cycle describes the major Earth materials, the processes that form them, and how they relate to each other.
Igneous rock forms when liquid rock freezes solid; lithified sediment becomes sedimentary rock; pre-existing rock can transform into metamorphic rock.
If conditions melt the rocks into magma, the cycle begins anew with new igneous rocks.
attribution: An Introduction to Geology (opengeology.org), §4 The rock cycle

artifact.df: A rock made when liquid rock solidifies into a new solid form.
artifact.eg: Magma cooling after a volcanic eruption can form igneous rock.
artifact.mi: Any rock formed at Earth’s surface is igneous.
artifact.cx: Surface formation alone does not make a rock igneous; the defining step is freezing from liquid rock.

artifact.df: The continuous transformation of Earth's three rock families.
artifact.eg: A granite (igneous) weathering into sandstone (sedimentary) and then into slate (metamorphic).
artifact.mi: Believing the cycle only involves the formation of igneous rocks.
artifact.cx: The cycle describes how igneous, sedimentary, and metamorphic rocks form and transform into one another.

claims: In music, form refers to the structure of a musical composition or performance.
The term "binary form" is used to describe a musical piece with two sections that are about equal in length.
Musical form unfolds over time through the expansion and development of these ideas.
Form in music is the result of the interaction of the four structural elements described above [sound, harmony, melody, rhythm].
Subdivisions of each large musical unit are shown by lowercase letters (a, b, and so on).
The next level concerns the entire structure of any single self-contained musical piece or movement.

artifact.q: How is the entire structure of a single self-contained musical piece or movement typically analyzed?
op: A) By analyzing only the melody
B) By examining the interaction of sound, harmony, melody, and rhythm
D) By looking only at sectional evidence
artifact.ex: B is correct because form is the result of the interaction of the four structural elements described above [sound, harmony, melody, rhythm]. C is a plausible misconception because binary form is a specific type of form, not the general method for analyzing the entire structure.

artifact.q: When analyzing a self-contained musical piece or movement, what level of organization is being described?
op: the entire structure of the piece
a single motive or short idea
the balance of sound and silence
artifact.ex: The entire structure of the piece is correct because this level concerns the full, self-contained musical piece or movement. A likely misconception is to focus on a small repeated idea or ending pattern, which describes a smaller unit rather than the whole form.

claims: Rhythm (from Greek ῥυθμός, rhythmos, "any regular recurring motion, symmetry") generally means a "movement marked by the regulated succession of strong and weak elements, or of opposite or different conditions".
"Meter may be defined as a regular, recurring pattern of strong and weak beats.
Triple metre is a metre in which each bar is divided into three beats, or a multiple thereof.

artifact.q: A passage is organized so that the beats recur in a regular pattern of strong and weak accents. Which description is most accurate?
artifact.ex: Meter is the regular, recurring pattern of strong and weak beats. Triple metre is a more specific kind of meter with three beats per bar, while progression is a harmonic idea, not a beat pattern.

artifact.q: Which term describes a regular, recurring pattern of strong and weak beats?
artifact.ex: Meter is defined as a regular, recurring pattern of strong and weak beats.

claims: In music, form refers to the structure of a musical composition or performance.
The term "binary form" is used to describe a musical piece with two sections that are about equal in length.
Musical form unfolds over time through the expansion and development of these ideas.
Form in music is the result of the interaction of the four structural elements described above [sound, harmony, melody, rhythm].
Subdivisions of each large musical unit are shown by lowercase letters (a, b, and so on).
The next level concerns the entire structure of any single self-contained musical piece or movement.

artifact.q: Which structural element describes the overall arrangement of a complete musical piece?
artifact.ex: Musical form is the result of the interaction of sound, harmony, melody, and rhythm. Binary form is a specific type of musical form with two equal sections. Musical form refers to the structure of a musical composition or performance. Chordal function relates to the role of chords within a piece.

artifact.q: Which choice best matches what musical form describes in a composition?
op: The overall structure of the piece
The number of chords in a phrase
The exact pitch pattern of a scale
The loudness level of each section
artifact.ex: The correct choice is the overall structure of the piece. A common misconception is to treat form as the chord count or another single surface feature, but form is the larger organization that unfolds over time; it results from the interaction of the musical elements, not just one of them.

claims: Interactive prototyping builds a testable representation of how a planned experience looks and works without requiring every production detail.
Prototypes can be combined with usability testing or a cognitive walkthrough to test whether a design concept works.
Functional prototypes allow a team to observe how users interact with a product.
A prototype should show the major interactions even when not every interaction is functional.
Prototypes should support fast iteration and be inexpensive enough to discard after learning from them.

artifact.df: A visual model of an experience used for testing.
artifact.eg: A low-fidelity wireframe showing the main navigation flow.
artifact.mi: A static drawing that requires no user interaction to evaluate.
artifact.cx: A visual model that can be tested for functionality and interaction.

artifact.df: Creating a testable stand-in for an experience so teams can evaluate how it looks and works without building every production detail.
artifact.eg: A team makes a clickable checkout prototype to test the main interactions before coding the full flow.
artifact.mi: It means a polished finished product.
artifact.cx: It is meant to be inexpensive and fast enough to discard after learning from it.

artifact.df: A version that lets people interact with the design so their behavior can be observed.
artifact.eg: A task-flow mockup lets users try the signup steps while the team watches where they hesitate.
artifact.mi: It only needs to look right on screen.
artifact.cx: It must support interaction well enough to observe how users use it.

artifact.df: Working models that allow users to observe interaction.
artifact.eg: A clickable mock-up where users can navigate through the main screens.
artifact.mi: A model that must show every interaction even when not functional.
artifact.cx: Models that allow a team to observe how users interact with a product.
